topic: Different Types of Volcanoes and Volcanic Eruptions
key_concepts: A volcano is an opening in Earth’s surface that allows lava, ash, and gases to escape.
Volcanism is the movement of magma toward or onto Earth’s surface.
A volcano’s main parts include summit, slopes, base, vent, crater, conduit, and magma cham
The magma chamber stores magma before an eruption; the conduit connects it to the crater.
Volcanoes are classified by structure as cinder cone, composite, shield, and lava dome.
Cinder cone volcanoes are the simplest type and are built from particles and blobs of lava
Composite volcanoes form from alternating layers of lava flow, ash, and rock fragments.
Shield volcanoes form from wide thin layers of fluid lava.
